items.title: FS70 / FS71 – All Other Entities Due 31 Oct 2026
items.desc: AFS licensees that are not disclosing entities must lodge FS70/71 (profit & loss, balance sheet, auditor's report) with ASIC by 31 October 2026. Annual financial report (Ch 2M) also due 31 Oct for non-disclosing entities.

items.title: Derivative Client Money Report – Due 31 Oct 2026
items.desc: AFSL holders with derivative retail client money must lodge the annual client money data report with ASIC by 31 October 2026.

items.title: Digital Asset No-Action Expired – Enforcement Now Active
items.desc: ASIC's no-action position for digital asset businesses expired 30 September 2026. Firms without an AFSL, variation, or authorised representative arrangement now risk civil and criminal penalties. ASIC has signalled active enforcement from 1 October 2026.

items.title: MDA Relief Replaced – Instrument 2026/720 in Effect
items.desc: ASIC replaced the managed discretionary account (MDA) relief with Instrument 2026/720 on 30 September 2026. Terms are largely unchanged — MDA providers and custodians should confirm their current arrangements remain compliant.

items.title: FAR Simplification – Consultation Closes End 2026
items.desc: APRA and ASIC are consulting on Financial Accountability Regime changes: dropping prescribed key functions from the register, raising change notification thresholds, and halving accountability map updates. Changes expected to commence early 2027.

items.title: Digital Assets Framework – Q4 Consultation Paper Expected
items.desc: ASIC's Digital Assets Framework roadmap anticipates a consultation paper on DAP/TCP licensing guidance in Q4 2026. AFSL applications for digital asset platforms open from 9 April 2027. Monitor ASIC news centre for release.

items.title: Tranche 2 Obligations Fully In Force – Enforcement Begins
items.desc: Lawyers, accountants, real estate professionals, conveyancers, jewellers and trust & company service providers have been subject to AML/CTF obligations since 1 July 2026. Enrolment deadline has passed. AUSTRAC enforcement focus now on non-enrolled entities.

items.title: Independent AML/CTF Program Review – 12-Month Deadline
items.desc: Higher-risk reporting entities must complete an independent review of their AML/CTF program within 12 months of the 31 March 2026 reform commencement — due by 31 March 2027. Begin scoping and engaging reviewers now.

items.title: VASP Travel Rule – In Effect for New Reporting Entities
items.desc: The travel rule for virtual asset transfers took effect for newly regulated VASPs from 1 July 2026. Entities involved in virtual asset transfers must now pass originator and beneficiary information with each transfer.

items.title: Annual Compliance Report – Next Due 30 Sep 2027
items.desc: No compliance report required for the Jan–Jun 2026 transition period. First report under the new FY cycle covers 1 Jul 2026 – 30 Jun 2027, due 30 September 2027. Begin building data collection processes now.

items.title: New TTR and SMR Forms – Transition Still Open
items.desc: Updated AUSTRAC threshold transaction and suspicious matter report forms remain available. Old forms valid until 30 March 2029. Entities should plan system upgrades within this transition window.

items.title: Quarterly Compliance Reports – Due 31 Oct 2026
items.desc: AER-regulated entities must submit quarterly compliance reports by 31 October 2026 covering the July–September 2026 quarter. Refer to AER Compliance Procedures and Guidelines Appendix A for applicable obligations.

items.title: AER 2026–27 Compliance & Enforcement Priorities Active
items.desc: AER's 2026–27 priorities are in effect: vulnerable consumer outcomes, smart meter rollout protection, power system security, network safety and competition, and Part 10 National Gas Rules reporting compliance.

items.title: Minimum Disconnection Amount Now $500
items.desc: AER raised the minimum amount before a retailer may disconnect a customer under NECF from $300 to $500, effective 1 July 2026. Confirm disconnection systems and procedures have been updated.

items.title: Rate of Return Instrument Review – Final Decision Dec 2026
items.desc: AER's 2026 RORI review is ongoing. Final decision expected December 2026, setting allowed returns on capital for regulated electricity and gas networks for the next regulatory cycle.

items.title: Exemptions Guidelines 2026 Review – Consultation Ongoing
items.desc: AER's review of the Exemptions Guidelines is ongoing. Proposes reduced regulatory burden for commercial embedded network retrofits to align with flexible trading reforms.
